text:
simon: Hey team, seeing big east-west p95/p99 latency spikes between GPU nodes during our nightly peak batching window (roughly 03:45-04:30 UTC). Starts right when batching density increases.
maya: ugh. symptoms? packet loss, retransmits, CPU saturation?
simon: p99 jumps from ~6ms → 80-150ms for inter-node RPCs. tcp_retrans shows small blips, but netstat tx-queue length spikes. not CPU-bound on inference processes.
chen: did we roll any NIC firmware or kernel changes last week? I remember a driver update on the 04 cluster.
anita: @chen we applied Broadcom firmware 3 days ago on 04-gpu-pools. infra-bot reported successful deploy, no rollback.
simon: i ran quick ethtool -S, see growing tx_dropped and lro/gro stats fluctuating. MTU still 1500 on most nodes.
maya: batching window increases packet rate; could be microbursts. might be small MTU + LRO/GRO interaction causing uneven offloads. try disabling GRO on a canary node?
chen: Agree. Also check if RDMA fallback is happening. Some kernels fall back to TCP when XPMEM or libibverbs hits errors. That would blow latency.
anita: infra-bot pulled logs: /var/log/kern.log shows repeated "mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: qedr: QP 0x... error -14" on two hosts around the same times.
simon: ok that's likely mlx5 IB issues. For immediate mitigation: reduce batch window to lower concurrency and spread requests across racks, and drain the two suspect hosts.
maya: can we config the scheduler to avoid packing large batches onto same rack during peak? a short-lived placement tweak might help while we troubleshoot NICs.
chen: running quick iperf3 between two GPU nodes during spike reproduces intermittent 100+ms jitter with packet loss. When I disabled GRO (ethtool -K eth0 gro off) jitter dropped to ~5-10ms, but CPU usage rose ~4%.
anita: so GRO/LRO offload interplay + NIC driver instability + microbursts. actionable list?
simon: Proposed: 1) Canary disable GRO on suspect hosts (done by chen). 2) Roll back Broadcom firmware on pool if driver regressions confirmed. 3) Tune batcher to lower max_batch_tokens from 4096→2048 during peak window. 4) Add rack-aware placement during 03:30-04:45 UTC. 5) Run RDMA health checks and ibv_devinfo; collect core dumps if mlx5 errors persist.
maya: also recommend bump MTU to 9000 on test rack and re-run iperf with RDMA enabled. Jumbo frames may reduce CPU interrupts and spread bursts, but need switch config.
chen: I captured tcpdump and ibdump. putting them in /tmp/ew-latency-capture.tar.gz. Sharing shortly.
anita: I'll open a short incident ticket and email ops@redwood-inference with mitigation plan. SLA impact low but customer-facing tails may be worse.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-17. Assigned: eng-infra, priority: P2. Attachments: /tmp/ew-latency-capture.tar.gz (chen).
simon: timeline: can we roll one mitigation (batch size cap + drain 2 hosts) in next 15m?
maya: yes, i'll prepare quick config patch for the batcher and submit canary deploy.
chen: disabling GRO on the two hosts now. monitoring metrics.
anita: I'll coordinate firmware rollback if infra-bot flags it as the root cause. also scheduling a deeper kernel/driver test on staging overnight.
simon: thanks. after we stabilize, let's run controlled experiments: MTU 1500 vs 9000, GRO on vs off, RDMA vs TCP, at different batch densities. collect p50/p95/p99 and CPU cost.
maya: noted. will add an eval job to the queue and tag results in the infra dashboard. :thumbsup:
simon: good. ping me if latency creeps back up.
chen: initial telemetry: p99 dropped back to ~9ms after GRO off. keeping watch for 30m.
anita: leaving this thread open until we're green for 6 hours. thanks all.
